description.value: The study examined whether younger and older adults use similar neural systems during cognitive reappraisal and whether age and individual differences in cognitive ability relate to emotion-regulation-related brain activation.

design.value: Older adults and younger adults completed a cognitive reappraisal task during fMRI scanning. Each participant attended two sessions on different days: a psychometric testing and training session followed by an fMRI scanning session. The study used a between-subjects age-group comparison with positive, negative, and neutral pictures and Experience and Reappraise task conditions.

description.value: Participants scored 27 or above on the Mini-Mental State Examination.
Participants viewed a series of 16 words, read each word aloud, and then verbally recalled as many words as possible at the end of the series.
Participants recalled as many of the 16 words as possible after a 20-min delay.
The 16 target words and 16 lure words were presented, and participants evaluated whether each word was old or new.
Participants pressed the spacebar every time a white square appeared in the middle of the screen; performance was calculated as mean reaction time for correct choices.
Participants pressed the corresponding left or right button when shown arrows pointing to the left or right; performance was calculated as mean reaction time for correct choices.

Participants responded to the color of the words art, game, red, and blue, presented in red or blue text. Performance included accuracy on congruent minus incongruent trials and the mean reaction-time difference between incongruent and congruent trials.

description.value: Participants listened to strings of numbers and recited each string in forward or backward order; the string length increased following two correct responses and the task ended after errors on two consecutive trials.

Subjects were assigned z scores for each cognitive measure relative to the mean and standard deviation of the younger subjects, and a single composite score was derived based on mean performance across all measures.

task_description.value: The first session included a psychometric testing battery and training on the emotional reappraisal paradigm. The battery included memory, response time, working memory, and Stroop tasks, followed by self-report measures of emotional functioning.

stimuli.value: 16 target words and 16 lure words, white squares, left- or right-pointing arrows, colored words, and strings of numbers.

task_description.value: Each trial began with a single photographic image that was negative, positive, or neutral in valence. Participants viewed the image for 2 s, received a 2-s verbal cue to experience their emotions naturally or decrease their emotional response by reappraising the image, and then continued implementing the cued strategy during a 6-s fixation and instruction period. At the end of each trial, participants rated the image's affective valence for 4 s.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed either to experience their emotions naturally or to decrease their emotional response to the image by reappraising it, using an emotionally detached and objective third-party strategy.

stimuli.value: Positive, neutral, and negative photographic images drawn from the International Affective Picture System. Positive images had a mean standardized valence rating of 7.3, neutral images 5.1, and negative images 2.5.

task_performance_measures.value: self-reported valence rating using an 8-option non-verbal Manikin scale

description.value: Functional data were collected across six runs using a gradient-echo inverse-spiral pulse sequence with standard BOLD fMRI parameters. Each run contained 238 imaging volumes. The first six volumes from each run were removed to allow stabilization of the T2 signal.

structured_details.value: {"field_of_view_mm": 240, "flip_angle_degrees": 90, "slices": 34, "slice_orientation": "axial slices parallel to the AC–PC plane", "runs": 6}

description.value: An initial high-resolution inversion-recovery-prepared SPGR anatomical scan was acquired to aid with co-registration and normalization, with whole-brain coverage.

Functional data were preprocessed with motion correction, slice-timing correction, removal of non-brain voxels, spatial smoothing, high-pass temporal filtering, run exclusion based on head motion, registration to high-resolution anatomical images, and normalization to the MNI template.

steps.value: removal of non-brain voxels using BET
spatial smoothing with a Gaussian kernel of FWHM 6 mm

model_settings.value: The model included five regressors of interest for Experience-Positive, Experience-Negative, Experience-Neutral, Reappraise-Positive, and Reappraise-Negative. These modeled the 8-s period of experiencing or reappraising emotional content using a unit amplitude function. Nuisance regressors modeled the 2-s visual presentation and response period. Analyses used whole-brain-corrected thresholds of voxel z > 2.3 and cluster-corrected P < 0.05.

software.value: FEAT Version 5.98, part of FSL (FMRIB's Software Library)

hrf_model.value: amygdala activation time courses were convolved with a boxcar task waveform

model_settings.value: The model included activation time courses from the left and right amygdala, a boxcar task regressor weighted positively for Reappraise trials and negatively for Experience trials, and two regressors of interest created from the convolution of each amygdala activation time course with the task regressor. Amygdala seed voxels were defined by the conjunction of Reappraise > Experience contrasts for positive and negative stimuli.

software.value: FEAT Version 5.98, part of FSL (FMRIB's Software Library)

model_settings.value: The relationship between activation changes in each ROI in the Reappraisal versus Experience contrast and the cognitive composite score was examined while controlling for the effects of age upon both cognition and ROI activation.

interpretations.value: Reappraisal of negative images evoked increased activation in prefrontal regions and decreased activation in the amygdala.
Reappraisal of positive images evoked increased activation in prefrontal regions and decreased activation in the amygdala.
